acceptance_criteria: AC-1 V8 creates local_credentials as contract section 3.2 states, and V1-V7 are untouched.
AC-2 The mechanism registry exists with local as a non-removable member, and adding ldap would be adding a member rather than changing the flow. State in the SESSION_CLOSE how that is true.
AC-3 Verification uses Argon2id with per-row parameters read from the row, not from a constant.
AC-4 A test proves every failure mode returns the identical response body, and a test proves the constant response-time envelope holds when verification is skipped due to lockout.
AC-5 Tests cover the lockout threshold, its effect, and its clearing.
AC-6 Password change works; no forced change exists anywhere in the code.
AC-7 Both bootstrap accounts are seeded on a clean database with their role bindings, and a test proves they are distinct actors in audit rows.
AC-8 A test proves no credential material -- password, verifier, salt or parameters -- appears in any audit row produced by any path this movement adds.
AC-9 A login screen exists and no product screen renders without a session; a frontend test proves it.
AC-10 The component-scan exclusion is narrowed deliberately and the SESSION_CLOSE states exactly what it now admits.
AC-11 ./ui2/gradlew -p ui2 build -x :integration-tests:test passes, architecture tests pass, and the module listing is still eleven.
AC-12 The repository privacy gate reports zero findings.
AC-13 No file under panorama/, configuration/, utils/, scripts/ or docs/design/ is modified.

Read all of it before writing anything.

Do not redesign, extend or work around any of it. docs/design/UI2_0_C1_PLATFORM_SCHEMA_CONTRACT.md (FROZEN) owns Flyway as sole migration authority, the fn_audit_capture trigger the new table attaches to, and the two database roles.

context_not_loaded: Check Point and Palo Alto contracts
invariants: No recoverable password exists anywhere in the product.
Local authentication can never be disabled.
A refusal never reveals whether an identity exists, in body or in timing.
No credential material reaches an audit row, a log line or an exception message.
Sessions, RBAC and audit behave exactly as C3 fixes them.
No product screen renders without a session.
The two bootstrap identities remain distinct actors in the audit trail.
Flyway history is append-only; no existing migration is edited.
report.merge_gate: Product Owner assistant review of the diff plus orchestrator verify.passed. The worker does not merge to main.
report.objective: Implement local authentication end to end against docs/design/UI2_0_C3A_LOCAL_AUTHENTICATION_CONTRACT.md (FROZEN 2026-09-13): the local_credentials table and its migration, the mechanism registry with local as its first member, login and lockout, password change, the two seeded bootstrap accounts, and a login screen that stands in front of the existing UI. The Product Owner's stated goal is that the product cannot be used without logging in, even on localhost.
output_contract: A product that cannot be used without logging in, with two distinct bootstrap identities.
A registry that admits LDAP later without rework.
Tests that prove the refusal is non-revealing in timing as well as in body, and that no credential material reaches audit.
SESSION_CLOSE naming which contract clause each new type implements, what the component-scan exclusion now admits, and the build/test counts before and after.

recommended_reasoning.reason: A security boundary implemented against a contract that is already explicit, so the design is decided -- but the failure modes are subtle: a timing side channel, parameters read from the wrong place, credential material leaking into audit. High effort for the care those need, not for the volume of code.

requirements: English, per AGENTS.md engineering-output language law.
Java written from scratch for the backend; the existing Python is know-how only and must not be read as a source to port.
Every public type and method carries a short comment naming the contract clause it implements. A clause with no code and code with no clause are both defects.
Do NOT use './ui2/gradlew -p ui2 build' without '-x :integration-tests:test'. The integration tests fail closed on a missing database by design; that is correct behaviour and not something to fix.
Do not run the full Python pytest suite. It creates untracked data/ and logs/ directories that the repository privacy gate then flags.
The ui2 build must keep exactly eleven Gradle subprojects.
Commit early and often: the migration, the registry and verification, login and lockout, the seeding, the screen, then the tests.
Do not merge to main. The Product Owner assistant reviews the diff and merges.
If the contract does not answer something, raise one RELAY_QUESTION rather than deciding it.
risks: Implementing the non-revealing refusal in the response body only and leaving the timing side channel open. Section 5.3 requires both and a skipped verification is measurably faster.
Reading Argon2 parameters from a constant instead of from the row, which defeats the whole point of recording them per row.
Adding a forced password change because it seems obviously right. The Product Owner deferred it deliberately and section 6.2 records why.
Editing an existing Flyway migration instead of adding V8.
Widening the component-scan exclusion more than the login flow needs.
Letting a verifier, salt or parameter set reach an audit row or a log line.
Redesigning sessions or RBAC because the login flow touches them.

in: The Flyway migration creating local_credentials exactly as contract section 3.2's DDL states, as V8. Do not renumber or edit any existing migration -- Flyway is sole migration authority and history is append-only.
The mechanism registry of contract section 2, with `local` as its first and non-removable member. The shape must make adding `ldap` later an added member, not a changed flow.

Credential verification using the Argon2id family with the per-row parameters the DDL records, so parameters can be raised later without invalidating existing rows. Never a reversible form, never a plain column, never a fast general-purpose digest.
Login and lockout per contract section 5: per-identity counting, the stated threshold, the stated lock duration and clearing rule.

The non-revealing refusal of section 5.3, INCLUDING the timing requirement. Every failure mode -- unknown identity, wrong password, empty password, active lockout -- returns the identical response AND is served inside a constant response-time envelope, so a skipped verification does not return measurably faster than a performed one. This is the clause most likely to be implemented in body only; implement the timing too.

Password change per section 4, available from the first release. There is NO forced change: the Product Owner deferred it on 2026-09-13 and section 6.2 records that decision, its risk and its revisit condition. Implement the ability, not a compulsion.

Seeding the two bootstrap accounts, nexusadmin and claudeadmin, on a clean empty database, with their role bindings per section 7. claudeadmin exists so automation actions are attributable to it rather than to the Product Owner; keep the two identities genuinely distinct in the audit trail.

Wiring LoginController and LoginResolveController into Ui2Application's component scan, and whatever else section 2's flow requires. Change the scan exclusion deliberately and say in the SESSION_CLOSE exactly what it now admits -- it was excluded for a reason and you are narrowing that exclusion, not deleting it.

A login screen in ui2/frontend: username and password, submit, and an error presentation that shows the same message for every failure mode, matching section 5.3. The application must not render any product screen until a session exists -- the six existing screens stay exactly as they are behind it.

Audit coverage per section 8: every authentication attempt, lockout, password change and role-binding change, through C1 section 3.5's existing mechanism. No credential, verifier, salt or parameter set may reach an audit row, a log line or an exception message.

Tests for contract section 11's specification, including at minimum: the non-revealing refusal including timing, lockout threshold and clearing, that no credential material appears in any audit row, that both bootstrap accounts exist and are distinct actors, and that a product screen is unreachable without a session.
out: LDAP, RADIUS or TACACS implementation. The registry must ADMIT ldap; nothing may be built for it. C3 owns LDAP and C-2 names RADIUS and TACACS as later.

Any forced password change, any password expiry, complexity class, history or reuse rule. The Product Owner explicitly deferred password policy on 2026-09-13. Implement only what section 4 requires for a password to be storable.
Redesigning or extending sessions, role tokens, role bindings, RBAC enforcement or the gate chain. C3 owns them and they are unchanged.
Editing any existing Flyway migration, or any FROZEN contract.
Any user-management screen -- creating, listing, disabling or editing accounts. Only login and password change are in scope.
Any device contact, any discovery, any Palo Alto or Check Point work.
Changing the Ingress, any Kubernetes manifest, or anything about external exposure. Contract section 9 reports an unresolved tension there and this movement must not resolve it.
Self-service password reset, email, multi-factor, or session-token cryptography.
